$comment: Pattern-language spec for agentic-kanban (Lilienthal Musterelemente + rules) — round 1 (2026-08-16). Consumed by code-metrics-skill/pattern-language/tools/pattern_edges.py. FIRST matching element wins — specific before general. Rules are allow-lists (runtime imports only; type-only imports are erased). Elements without a rule entry (server-root, server-script, server-cli, server-worker, server-scaffold, client-route) are unconstrained. Seeded from .dependency-cruiser.cjs (routes/cli-not-down-to-persistence, services-bypass-repositories, repositories-are-infra-pure, services-not-up-to-routes, client-hooks-not-up-to-components-or-routes, client-lib-is-leaf, shared-is-a-leaf, mcp-no-server-internals) — this spec ADDS what depcruise doesn't cover: startup/monitor, lib, scripts, worker.

elements.name: server-root
elements.intent: Composition root — boots the server: migrations, startup tasks, route mount, background-service registry, process handlers, readiness. The only place that wires everything together.

elements.name: server-monitor
elements.intent: Startup-owned engines and background sweeps: the in-process monitor (auto-start/merge/exit workflow) and crash-safe periodic reconcilers registered by name in BACKGROUND_SERVICES.

elements.name: server-script
elements.intent: One-shot executables under src/scripts/ — maintenance and migration helpers; unconstrained downward, never imported by anything.

elements.name: server-route
elements.intent: Thin Hono adapters: parse the request, delegate to a service, shape the response. No business logic, no drizzle.

elements.name: server-middleware
elements.intent: Cross-cutting request plumbing: createRouter, domainErrorHandler, parseJsonBody, gzip, slow-request sampling.

elements.name: server-repository
elements.intent: Pure drizzle access per use-case slice (not per table): verbNoun(args, database = db). No decisions, no side effects beyond the DB.

elements.name: server-service
elements.intent: Business logic and orchestration — factories createXService(deps) and fn-modules; gates, resolvers, reconcilers, adapters/ports, projections. Owns decisions; may use repositories, lib, db, shared.

elements.name: server-worker
elements.intent: The remote worker (fleet) process — dials the board, executes assignments in its own checkout, streams output back.

elements.name: server-cli
elements.intent: CLI command registrars (pnpm cli -- …): register a commander action that runs migrations, calls repos/services or the live REST API, and exits.

elements.name: server-scaffold
elements.intent: Artefacts SHIPPED into other repos: hook scripts and skill content copied into registered projects' .claude/. Must not import server internals.

elements.name: server-db
elements.intent: DB bootstrap: connection, migrations, pragmas, backup/repair, seed.

elements.name: server-lib
elements.intent: Pure server-side compute extracted to be unit-testable without a server: formatters, projections, small helpers. Imports no services, ideally no node:/db.

elements.name: shared-schema
elements.intent: Drizzle table definitions and the column vocabularies (as const) that live next to them — the one source of truth for the DB shape.

elements.name: shared-types
elements.intent: Type-only contracts shared between packages; no runtime code.

elements.name: shared-barrel
elements.intent: The package facade — the ONE module whose job is to union the three sub-barrels (schema, types, lib) for external consumers (421 importers reach `@agentic-kanban/shared`). Re-exporting `schema/` is what it is FOR, so it is its own element rather than a `shared-lib` member with a standing exception (#869). Internal shared modules never import it (that would be a cycle); only the other packages may.

elements.name: shared-db-op
elements.intent: A drizzle operation in packages/shared/src/lib that is the SINGLE write/cascade authority for a domain fact, shared by server AND mcp (mcp-no-server-internals forbids mcp importing server code). The only sub-kind of shared/lib permitted to value-import drizzle-orm and reach shared/schema; every other sub-kind (node-adapter, key-derivation, contract-codec, stream-parser, pure-policy/projection, telemetry-singleton) is pure with respect to persistence. Enumerated by path because the spec engine matches paths, not imports - shared-lib-sub-kinds.test.ts re-derives the set from the imports and fails on drift.

elements.name: shared-lib
elements.intent: Code used by more than one package, in seven sub-kinds: node-adapter (git/docker/fs, deep-path only), key-derivation, contract-codec, stream-parser, pure-policy/projection, telemetry-singleton - and shared-db-op, which is split out as its own element because it is the ONLY one allowed to touch persistence. Everything matching THIS element is pure with respect to the DB: no drizzle-orm, no shared/schema tables.

elements.name: mcp-tool
elements.intent: MCP tool handlers — the board's agent-facing API. Reach the board via shared lib/db ops or HTTP, never via server internals.

elements.name: client-route
elements.intent: Client-side routing: URL ↔ view derivation and the router mount.

elements.name: client-component
elements.intent: React UI. Renders state, dispatches actions via hooks/stores/lib; no persistence knowledge beyond the REST/WS surface.

elements.name: client-hook
elements.intent: Reusable client behaviour and data access (useX): fetching, subscriptions, derived state.

elements.name: client-store
elements.intent: Zustand stores — shared client state that more than one distant component drives.

elements.name: client-lib
elements.intent: Pure client helpers: API client, formatting, chart colours, registries; no React rendering.
